item.title: UN Reports Supersized’ El Niño May Become Strongest Ever Recorded
item.description: The El Niño weather phenomenon is set to intensify further into 2027 and could be the strongest ever, raising risks of extreme weather into next year, the World Meteorological Organization said on Thursday. “El Niño is being supersized before our eyes. weather agency said its forecasts showed a near 100% likelihood that El Niño would persist through February 2027, fueled by exceptionally warm Pacific Ocean temperatures.

item.title: Root Cites Legal Reforms for 15% Florida Auto Insurance Rate Reduction
item.description: Florida insurance reforms are being cited for a reduction in rates to drivers in the state as litigation costs decline, according to Root Insurance. “Florida’s insurance market continues to improve as costs continue to decline under the reforms, and Root’s ability to accurately price risk allows us to reflect those improvements in what our customers pay,” said Alex Timm, founder and CEO of Root. Last week, the tech-driven car insurer announced new rates that will reduce auto insurance premiums for Florida customers by 15% on average, with some policyholders seeing more significant decreases.

item.title: Global Venture Funding Jumps 122% In August As Streak Of Billion-Dollar Deals Continues
item.description: Two of August’s billion-dollar recipients illustrate the trend: Databricks added $56 billion to its valuation in just six months, while River AI raised both its seed and Series A rounds this year, amassing a staggering $1.1 billion in early-stage funding. That accelerated cadence extended across August’s megadeals: Five of the seven billion-dollar funding recipients had last raised capital less than 12 months earlier, including three that closed their previous rounds earlier this year. Venture investors poured $42 billion into just over 1,500 startups worldwide in August, Crunchbase data shows, down 25% from July’s $56 billion but still up a significant 122% compared to last August, which is typically a slower month for startup investment.

item.title: Howden Re urges reinsurance and retro cedents to preserve capital flexibility and optionality
item.description: In a reinsurance and retrocession market environment where prices have softened considerably but underwriters can still find attractive returns, broker Howden Re urges cedents to ensure their resilience by looking across the full-range of capital solutions and forms, to maintain flexibility and optionality through cycles. Diversification, optionality and alternative capital are all to be considered by cedents in the current reinsurance market environment, Howden Re says. While, for reinsurance capital providers, it’s a time to direct capacity to where risk-adjusted returns continue to support value creation, while retaining the flexibility to redeploy as conditions evolve.

item.title: New capital sources and risk dynamics create significant opportunities for growth: Oak Global CEO
item.description: As the insurance-linked securities (ILS) and reinsurance markets adapt to an evolving risk landscape spanning geopolitics, climate, and artificial intelligence (AI), new capital structures are emerging to meet growing demand, and Oak Global plans to leverage investor diversification to capture these opportunities, according to CEO and Founder, Cathal Carr. To begin, Carr shared with Artemis what Oak Global’s long-term goals are for scaling third-party capital. “We can also move to weather and climate-related risk and the increasing contribution of losses that are coming from secondary perils and the dynamic that continues to be at play there, and then we also need to think about technology and the impact that AI will have around existing products in terms of some of the casualty products that may be impacted by AI, but also new products that are emerging as a result of AI too.” Highlighting these distinct risk areas, Carr emphasised that it shows that there is a big challenge for the industry in terms of the evolving nature of those risks “But we view those as a significant opportunity for our industry, where there is growing demand and there is a significant protection gap within those areas of risks that we as an industry can grow within,” the CEO said.

item.title: Swiss Re names Wiget to take over leadership of Alternative Capital Partners
item.description: Swiss Re, the global reinsurer, has named long-standing senior employee Mirjam Wiget as the new leader for its Alternative Capital Partners (ACP) division, as incumbent Martin Zingg moves into the Group Chief Investment Officer role. Alternative Capital Partners (ACP) was established by Swiss Re in 2019 as a division to oversee all activities with alternative capital investors, as well as in the catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities (ILS) market, including its structuring and ILS fund management operations. Martin Zingg became the head of Swiss Re’s Alternative Capital Partners (ACP) division earlier this year , but since then he has been promoted to become Group CIO.

item.title: MS Transverse expands board
item.description: MS Transverse, a specialty insurance platform that works with programme administrators and managing general agents (MGAs), has strengthened its Board of Directors with the appointment of Michael Angelina, Bryan Sanders and Kevin Traetow. “We are pleased to welcome Michael, Bryan and Kevin to the MS Transverse board,” commented John Fitzgerald, Chief Executive Officer of MS Transverse. “Their combined experience across specialty insurance, reinsurance and actuarial risk management strengthens our board as we continue to build our partnership platform and grow our position in the market.” Angelina joins the MS Transverse board following a four-decade career spanning actuarial, risk management and senior leadership positions within the insurance sector.

item.title: Swiss Re sees cyber insurance growth opportunity as AI and rising risks reshape market
item.description: Swiss Re, the global reinsurance company, has examined how evolving cyber threats and gaps in insurance protection are influencing the market and its prospects for future growth in its latest analysis of the cyber insurance sector. Swiss Re’s assessment suggests that while the factors driving growth within the cyber insurance market have changed relatively little over the past year, the wider risk environment facing businesses has continued to develop. Despite the changing risk environment, Swiss Re reports that global cyber insurance premium growth continues to sit within the single-digit range.

item.title: Gallagher expands EMEA private capital and M&A team with senior commercial hire
item.description: Gallagher, the global insurance broking and risk management group, has strengthened its Private Equity and M&A (PEMA) operation in EMEA with the appointment of Paul Jeroen van de Grampel as Chief Commercial Officer EMEA. Based in London, van de Grampel will work across the EMEA region as Gallagher continues to develop its specialist offering for private capital investors, corporate buyers and participants in the M&A advisory market. The appointment comes alongside two further senior hires intended to strengthen the operational side of Gallagher’s EMEA PEMA business.

item.title: Trump Says Iran Strikes to Be Short, Asserts Hormuz Control
item.description: President Donald Trump said renewed attacks on Iran would likely be short-lived, reiterating his claim that the US controls the crucial Strait of Hormuz after fresh fighting spiked energy prices and rekindled fears of an open-ended war. The US military carried out a second round of strikes in three days overnight, targeting radar systems and mine-laying capabilities along Iran’s southern coast. “We took out all of the new equipment that they tried to build along the Strait of Hormuz — some defensive, some offensive,” Trump said.

item.title: Thomson Reuters Detects Cyber Incident, Says Unauthorized Party Accessed Files
item.description: A subsequent investigation by Thomson Reuters found that an unauthorized party obtained certain C-Track files in March, the company said on a website created to provide information about the incident. A unit of Thomson Reuters detected a cybersecurity incident in 11 U.S. The statement from the chief justices of the Court of Appeal for Ontario, the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, and the Ontario Court of Justice said Thomson Reuters detected unauthorized activity in one of its cloud environments, and had taken steps to contain the activity, working with Ontario’s Ministry of the Attorney General and the courts.

item.description: “With the rapidly softening market cycle, particularly in North American property, we’ve taken the decision” on Avatar, Santam Chief Executive Officer Tavaziva Madzinga said in an interview Thursday. 1 and will allow Santam to underwrite property, marine, energy, cyber and political risk. has paused its foray into the US as a decline in property premium rates in the world’s biggest economy forced South Africa’s largest general insurer to rethink its expansion plan.

item.title: New research examines insurance’s verification gap amid rapid AI adoption
item.description: Reserving against a risk not yet named Industry research published in March 2026, based on a survey of 300 US insurance claims professionals, found that 98% agree AI editing tools are driving a rise in digital media fraud, while just 32% say they are very confident they could identify a deepfake. Insurers are automating decisions faster than they are building the infrastructure needed to verify the information behind them, according to new research from Clearspeed, the voice-based risk assessment provider. The report, “The Speed of Trust: Building the Trust Intelligence Layer for Insurance in the Age of Agentic AI”, was commissioned by Clearspeed and independently authored by insurance innovation strategist Sabine VanderLinden, chief executive officer of Alchemy Crew Ventures.

item.title: Lloyd’s reports solid H1 2026 results as GWP rise 7% amid softening rates
item.description: “The syndicates operating in the Lloyd’s market delivered a solid aggregate set of results for the six months ended 30 June 2026. Lloyd’s has recorded a 6.9% rise in gross written premium (GWP) to £34.7bn for the first half of 2026, up from £32.5bn in H1 2025. For the first half of 2026, Lloyd’s generated profit before tax of £3.5bn, a decrease on the prior-year period’s £4.2bn.

item.title: Andrew Hare appointed chief executive officer of Japan, Marsh Re
item.description: Marsh has announced the appointment of Andrew Hare as chief executive officer of Japan, Marsh Re, effective 1 January 2027, subject to regulatory approval. As chief executive officer of Japan, Marsh Re, he will be responsible for overseeing client management and setting strategic initiatives to grow the business in the country. Hare will relocate to Tokyo from Singapore in mid-2027 and will report to Tony Gallagher, chief executive officer, Asia Pacific, Marsh Re.

item.title: Samsung insurers plan to buy Canopius
item.description: The Samsung insurers currently own 40% of Canopius. According to a report, Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance and Samsung Life Insurance are planning to acquire London-based (re)insurer Canopius Group by purchasing an additional 50% stake for more than $1.47 billion. The South Korean insurers are expected to sign a deal with major share owners including asset manager Centerbridge Partners.

item.title: SafePoint invests in Arrow Risk Management
item.description: SafePoint Holdings has acquired a minority stake in UK specialty MGA Arrow Risk Management, marking the US insurer’s first international partnership. Arrow will continue to be led by founders Jon Godfray, Mark Harrington and Lloyd Howson, while SafePoint international underwriting chief Chris Sharp will join its board. The companies plan to support Arrow’s existing underwriting practices, recruit additional specialist teams and develop relationships with new insurance and reinsurance capacity providers.

item.title: World acquires Pellechio Family Agency
item.description: World Insurance Associates acquired the business of Pellechio Family Agency, a Parsippany, New Jersey-based insurance agency, on May 1, 2026. The agency said joining World will allow it to offer additional products and services to clients. Giordano, Halleran & Ciesla advised World, while Castano Quigley Cherami represented Pellechio.

item.title: Florida Bans Flock Cameras, License Plate Readers From State Roads
item.description: Florida banned local police from installing license-plate readers on state roads, responding to growing concern about the proliferation of surveillance cameras made by Flock Safety and other companies. Miami Beach Mayor Steven Meiner argued that license-plate readers have helped police, calling it a “hit to public safety.” FDOT just revoked permits for Automated License Plate Readers (LPRs) on state roads, giving us 30 days to rip out technology that’s helped our Police track fleeing suspects, get guns off our streets, and arrest violent criminals. The Florida Department of Transportation on Monday revoked all permits for local law-enforcement agencies to operate license-plate reader systems, ordering any that have been installed removed from state roadways within 30 days.

item.title: Justice Department Pursuing Hackers Behind Attack On X Users
item.description: Justice Department is working with Elon Musk’s X to track down those behind an attempted password-recovery attack targeting hundreds of thousands of users of the social media platform this week, U.S. A password-recovery attack generally refers to attempts at gaining access to online accounts through the “forgot password” or account-recovery process. Blanche, in a statement on X, said “sophisticated cyber criminals” attempted the attack but it was disrupted by the platform.

item.title: 5 Reasons AI Rollouts Stall in Claims and How to Avoid Them
item.description: Here are the five places rollouts get stuck in claims review, and what tends to get them moving again. Everyone is talking about AI and claims teams know that they need to be doing something with it. Sometimes the honest answer really is bad timing – a bodily injury claims unit six months into migrating to a new claims management system, doesn’t have the people to run a pilot right now.

item.title: FCA decides to ban and fine Daniel Thomas over unauthorised pension transfer advice
item.description: The FCA has decided to ban Daniel Thomas from working in financial services and fine him £742,700 after finding he recklessly gave defined benefit pension transfer advice he was neither qualified nor allowed to give. Over 5 years Mr Thomas advised 53 clients about 63 transfers out of defined benefit pension schemes and is believed to have earned more than £173,000 in fees. Mr Thomas provided misleading information to his principal firm about his involvement in the pension transfer cases.

item.title: Bermuda’s life & annuity sidecar market hits $375bn amid rising private-market strategies: Morningstar DBRS
item.description: The life and annuity sidecar market in Bermuda has experienced rapid growth over the last several years, as insurers continue to scale up and expand beyond legacy blocks. However, Morningstar DBRS suggests that this momentum can also be viewed alongside the growth of rated feeder funds, as both structures highlight how insurance capital is increasingly being deployed into private-market strategies. Meanwhile, Chariot Reinsurance (Chariot Re), a Bermuda-based life and annuity reinsurance sidecar company launched by MetLife, Inc.

item.title: Challenger Life’s cat bond investments meet benchmark. Calix Re adds new dimension
item.description: Challenger Life reported that its insurance-linked securities (ILS) investments, predominantly catastrophe bonds, performed in-line with their benchmark over the last year, while the company also launched a new Bermuda life and annuity reinsurance entity named Calix Re, adding a new insurance-linked dimension for the company. With its life settlements allocation now completely wound down and its reinsurance sidecar investment having dwindled to only an AU $3 million valuation by the middle of this year, the catastrophe bond investments are the main ILS allocation for Challenger at this time. In US dollar terms, this means the total insurance-linked strategies allocation of Challenger Life rose from just under US $482 million at the end of last year, to a new valuation of just over US $508 million at June 30th 2026, with the catastrophe bond investments the sole driver given the sidecar investment declined in value slightly (this may also be in run-off).

item.title: Verisk launches U.S. Data Center Exposure Database
item.description: Recognising the burgeoning interest in underwriting exposures related to the data center build-out, global data analytics and technology provider Verisk has announced the launch of a dedicated exposure database for these large risks in the United States. Data Center Exposure Database is “designed to help insurers, reinsurers and brokers better understand and manage one of the fastest-growing concentrations of risk.” The opportunity is meaningful, given industry reports suggest global data center insurance premiums could more than double from around $10 billion in 2026 to as much as $23 billion by 2030. Verisk’s new exposure database provides building-level geocoding, facility footprints, physical characteristics and operational attributes for over 2,500 facilities across the United States.

item.title: Corgi Insurance launches reinsurance platform, Corgi Re
item.description: Corgi Insurance, the AI-native, full-stack insurer, has launched Corgi Re, a reinsurance platform designed to bring underwriting technology, speed, and operational efficiency to the reinsurance market. Jeremy Eisemann , Head of Government Affairs & Deputy General Counsel, Corgi Insurance, commented, “Reinsurance is one of the hardest markets to enter for a reason. With this launch, Corgi is expanding its role in the insurance industry to provide capacity and risk management solutions to insurers themselves.

item.title: Tiernan calls for innovation to become Lloyd’s ‘natural operating rhythm’
item.description: In a statement accompanying Lloyd’s H1 2026 results, Chief Executive Patrick Tiernan suggested that addressing challenges such as the protection and perception gaps will require the full power of the Lloyd’s market to be harnessed to manage risks that others cannot, moving beyond isolated innovations in products, capital or structures to make innovation the market’s natural operating rhythm. Even in advanced economies, some risks have become too expensive for many households and businesses to reasonably bear.” Tiernan said government or state-backed schemes had played an important role in cushioning the impact of extreme-tail and systemic events, pointing to TRIA and Pool Re for terrorism, and NFIP and Flood Re for flood risk. According to Tiernan, the insurance industry is continually challenged about the protection gap, which is the widening difference between economic losses and insured losses.

item.title: Substantial deterioration in underwriting or financial conditions required to reverse softening momentum: Howden Re
item.description: Reinsurance broker Howden Re has said that a substantial deterioration in underwriting or financial conditions would be required to reverse the reinsurance market’s current softening momentum. Howden Re suggests that, in the absence of a major shock, strong underwriting profitability and capital accumulation support the reinsurance market’s continued softening momentum. However, Howden Re suggests that a weakening in the wider financial or macroeconomic environment could reduce the market’s capacity to absorb underwriting volatility, leaving it more exposed to future shocks.

item.title: Samsung-Affiliated Insurers Plan to Buy Canopius for $1.5 Billion, Newspaper Says
item.description: South Korea’s Samsung Group-affiliated insurers plan to acquire London-based reinsurance company Canopius by buying an additional 50% stake for more than 2 trillion won ($1.47 billion), the Korea Economic Daily said on Thursday. are expected to sign a deal with major share owners including asset manager Centerbridge Partners, it added , citing unnamed industry sources. (Reporting by Jack Kim, Heekyong Yang; editing by Chris Reese and Sherry Jacob-Phillips)

item.title: UN Warns Global Warming Will Exceed 1.5C and Must Be Reversed
item.description: Since countries signed onto the 2015 Paris Agreement, the United Nations has regularly reported on the world’s progress at limiting global warming to 1.5C above pre-industrial levels. The world will likely surpass 1.5C in the next few years, it says, and warming will peak at around 1.8C in the best-case scenario. Without changes to current policies, warming could reach roughly 2.6C.

item.title: People Moves: Silva to Succeed Retiring Welch as Amica Chief Claims Officer
item.description: Silva to Succeed Retiring Welch as Amica SVP and Chief Claims Officer Amica Mutual Insurance Co. , headquartered in Lincoln, Rhode Island, announced that Sean Welch , senior vice president and chief claims officer, will retire at the end of the year following a 41-year career with the company. Effective December 1, Acel Silva will succeed Welch in the role.

item.title: Bridgepoint takes majority stake in Delegated Authority platform VIPR Solutions
item.description: Bridgepoint has completed a new majority investment in VIPR Solutions (VIPR), the insurance-native technology platform for Delegated Authority intelligence. The investment was made via Bridgepoint Growth, the firm’s small-cap fund focused on supporting the global expansion of rapidly growing businesses, which has become the majority shareholder in VIPR. At the forefront of Delegated Authority technology since 2009 and headquartered in London, VIPR sits at the heart of how the insurance market exchanges program business data.

Amwins (Charlotte, N.C.) has acquired Joseph Chiarello & Co. “Chiarello has built the gold standard in a highly technical, often overlooked niche,” comments Ryan Armijo, President, Amwins Underwriting.

item.title: Labor Day Travelers Face Higher Costs, Heavier Traffic: AAA
item.description: Labor Day travelers face heavier traffic, higher fuel, airfare, and hotel costs this year, according to AAA. The Top Labor Day Travel Destinations for 2026: Seattle, WA Orlando, FL Boston, MA Denver, CO New York, NY Chicago, IL Anaheim/Los Angeles, CA Las Vegas, NV Anchorage, AK Atlanta, GA Rome, Italy Vancouver, Canada London, England Dublin, Ireland Paris, France Calgary, Canada Barcelona, Spain Athens, Greece Amsterdam, Netherlands Halifax, Canada Labor Day Travel Costs Rise for Flights and Hotels Travelers are paying more for several major components of a Labor Day vacation this year. For travelers flying to the most popular Labor Day destinations, airfare is nearly 20% higher than last year, averaging $790.

item.title: AIG Executive Chair and Former CEO Zaffino Set to Exit for Palantir
item.description: AIG said early Wednesday that its former chief executive officer and current executive chair Peter Zaffino will be leaving the board effective Sept. Zaffino had just transitioned to the position of executive chair on June 1. To take his place on the board, AIG said John Rice, lead independent director, will serve as chair when Zaffino departs.

item.title: Former Apple Engineers’ Physical AI Startup Lyte Raises $165M At $1.6B Valuation
item.description: Lyte , a physical AI startup building sensing and perception technology for robots, has raised $165 million in Series C funding at a $1.6 billion post-money valuation. The Sunnyvale, California-based company was founded in 2021 by Alexander Shpunt , Arman Hajati and Yuval Gerson — a trio of former Apple engineers who worked on the iPhone giant’s advanced sensing and perception technologies. Shpunt had also previously co-founded PrimeSense , a startup whose 3D-sensing technology powered Microsoft Kinect before Apple acquired the company in 2013.

item.title: US and Bermuda reinsurers maintain profitability as premium growth slows: AM Best
item.description: AM Best, the credit rating agency and provider of insurance industry data and analysis, has reported that a group of leading US and Bermuda reinsurers remained underwriting profitable for a fifth consecutive year in 2025, despite a significant slowdown in premium growth. The findings are contained in AM Best’s latest Best’s Market Segment Report, US & Bermuda Reinsurers Maintain Strong Performance Despite Softening Market . AM Best said the sharp reduction in growth reflects a more cautious approach from reinsurers as market conditions become softer.

item.title: People: Builders Insurance Names Jasmund Board Chairman
item.description: Atlanta-based Builders Insurance Group has named David Jasmund, a longtime board member and investment banker, as chairman of the board. Jasmund has served on the Builders board since 2009. Jasmund succeeds Charles Potok, who retired last month after three years as chairman, the company said in a news release.

item.title: US-Iran Clashes Escalate as Fears Grow of Extended Conflict
item.description: Fighting between the US and Iran over control of the Strait of Hormuz intensified after a period of relative calm, triggering a fresh jump in energy prices as fears grow of an open-ended war. The US military carried out a second round of strikes in three days overnight, targeting radar systems and mine-laying capabilities along Iran’s southern coast. Iran retaliated with drone and missile volleys on US bases across the Middle East, in line with a pattern used throughout the six-month war.

item.title: Amwins Acquires Firearms Insurance Specialist Joseph Chiarello & Co.
item.description: Specialty insurance wholesale broker Amwins reports it has acquired Joseph Chiarello & Co., Inc., a managing general agent (MGA) specializing in commercial insurance for the firearms industry. Founded in 1934 and now led by third-generation family members Joseph and Stephen Chiarello, the company has spent more than 40 years building its reputation in firearms industry insurance, serving more than 4,000 businesses. Chiarello will join Amwins Underwriting, adding a new area of specialty expertise to the division’s program portfolio.

item.title: Root and Carvana extend embedded insurance partnership to 2028
item.description: Root Insurance has announced the extension of its embedded partnership with Carvana to at least August 2028. Alex Timm, founder and chief executive officer of Root Insurance, said the renewal reflected the strength of the programme. In less than four years, the partnership has surpassed 200,000 policies sold.

item.title: Insurance's Gap in Identity Security
item.description: Partner ecosystems are the identity security gap that most financial institutions, including insurers, have yet to close. Research from Enterprise Strategy Group (ESG) , commissioned by Thales, found that 74% of BFSI organizations, spanning banking, insurance, and financial services, report third-party identities growing faster than employee identities, with third-party identity volumes projected to grow 37% over the next 12 months. The operational signals emerging from partner identity environments increasingly look like security warnings.

item.description: The Bermuda-based Class E life and annuity reinsurer plans to use the financing to expand its capacity for a growing pipeline of reinsurance opportunities. The financing expands our capacity to scale the reinsurance platform while maintaining our focus on disciplined underwriting and policyholder protection.” – Cynthia Smith, Chief Executive Officer of Chariot Re. MetLife and General Atlantic, Chariot Re’s sponsors, participated in the round, alongside institutional investors led by Chubb.
